DILG • Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph 07 ÜfLG OPINION NO. Od FEDERICO R. ALDECOA 22 Zamboanga St., Brgy. Nayong Kanluran Quezon City Dear Mr. Aldecoa: This has reference to an electronic mail ("e-mail") you sent dated 15 October 2019, seeking this Department's legal opinion concerning the plan of your barangay in enacting an ordinance requiring its residents to obtain car stickers for its vehicles as a security measure and enable the barangay officials to regulate the entry of non- resident vehicles even though it is not a private subdivision. At the outset, this Department acknowledges the fact that an ordinance has yet to be enacted by the Sangguniang Barangay and that, in previous legal opinions of this Department, it has already opined that inasmuch as an ordinance has undergone the procedural process for its enactment under the LGC, the same is considered valid unless decreed otherwise by our courts of justice. Any issues or questions thereon as to the substantive validity and enforceability of an ordinance should be threshed out by filing the appropriate special civil action for declaratory relief before the proper court in accordance with the Rules of Court. Be that as it may, since you mentioned in your e-mail that your main concern is to express your sentiments and to find out whether it has basis, we deemed it proper to tackle your concern for academic purposes. As to the validity of an ordinance, the Supreme Court, in several casesl, has made a pronouncement that for municipal ordinances to be valid, it: (a) must not contravene the Constitution or any other statute; (b) must not be unfair or oppressive; (c) must not be discriminatory; (d) must not prohibit, but may regulate trade; (e) must not be unreasonable; and (f) must be general in application and consistent with public policy. Furthermore, this Department has issued an opinion2 regarding the basic requisites of a valid ordinance, to wit: "At the outset, in the review of an ordinance, the basic rule is that the subject of the ordinance must not be violative 1 Tatel v. Municipality of Virac, GR No. 40243, March 11, 1992; Magtajas v. Pryce Properties, GR No. 111097, July 20, 1994 2 DILG Legal Opinion NO. 45, S.2018 dated 26 July 2018

of any national laws and the passage or amendment thereof must be within the corporate powers of the city to enact, and must be in accordance with the procedure prescribed by law, the Local Government Code (LGC)' Similar with cities, under the LGC, the barangays, have been given power to enact ordinances, through its respective Sangguniang Barangays3, in order to discharge its duty of promoting the general welfare of its inhabitants. For this reason, it is imperative for the Sangguniang Baranggay to observe the requisites in enacting an ordinance. We now delve on the issue regarding the imposition of car stickers which you believe is a form of tax on all vehicles as a security measure and whether its exercise is within the limits prescribed under the law. As to the first limitation, the desired purpose of your Barangay in enacting the ordinance is to serve as a security measure as the barangay will be able to regulate the entry of non-resident vehicles. On that premise, this Department recognizes the power of the local government units ("LGUs") to regulate the use of property and the enjoyment of life and liberty for the common good. This refers to the adoption of measures that it considers necessary and proper to promote health and safety, to maintain peace and order, and to preserve the well-being of its inhabitants, among others. As to the second limitation, the same is within the limits prescribed by the LGC. Section 391(a)(2) provides that the sangguniang barangay, as the legislative body of the barangay, shall enact tax and revenue ordinances, subject to the limitations imposed in this Code. Moreover, Section 1554 of the LGC also allows the sanggunian concerned to prescribe terms and conditions and fix the rates for the imposition of toll fees or charges for the use of any public road funded and constructed by the local government unit concerned. Hence, as long as the foregoing requisites are observed, this Department believes that the said barangay may enact such ordinance. On the other hand, we agree on your argument that since the streets belong to the general public and therefore the barangay should not be allowed to prevent 3 SECTION 48. Local Legislative Power. — Local legislative power shall be exercised by the Sangguniang panlalawigan for the province; the sangguniang panlungsod for the city; the sangguniang bayan for the municipality; and the sangguniang barangay for the barangay. 4 SECTION 155. Toll Fees or Charges. — The Sanggunian concerned may prescribe the terms and conditions and fix the rates for the imposition of toll fees or charges for the use of any public road, pier, or wharf, waterway, bridge, ferry or telecommunication system funded and constructed by the local government unit concerned: Provided, That no such toll fees or charges shall be collected from officers and enlisted men of the Armed Forces of the Philippines and members of the Philippine National Police on mission, post office personnel delivering mail, physically- handicapped, and disabled citizens who are sixty-five (65) years or older. When public safety and welfare so requires, the sanggunian concerned may discontinue the collection of the tolls, and thereafter the said facility shall be free and open for public use.

residents and non-residents of the barangay from using it or from passing through it, except in cases of permanent and/or temporary closure pursuant to Section 21(d)5 of the LGC. In the same vein, in case the barangay would prohibit vehicles without the stickers to enter the barangay, making the ordinance no longer a mere revenue- raising measure but a regulatory measure, such would be violative Of the provisions of the LGC as it is the city itself that has the power to regulate the roadways, to wit: SECTION 458. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. — (a) The sangguniang panlungsod, as the legislative body of the city, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the genera/ welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the city as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shall: xx xxx xxx (5) Approve ordinances which shall ensure the efficient and effective delivery of the basic services and facilities as provided for under Section 17 of this Code, and in addition to said services and facilities, shall: xxx xxx xxx (v) Regulate the use of streets, avenues, alleys, sidewalks, bridges, parks and other public places and approve the construction, improvement, repair and maintenance of the same; establish bus and vehicle stops and terminals or regulate the use of the same by privately-owned vehicles which serve the public; regulate garages and the operation of conveyances for hire; designate stands to be occupied by public vehicles when not in use; regulate the putting up of signs, signposts, awnings and awning posts on the streets; and provide for the lighting, cleaning and sprinkling of streets; and public places; (vi) Regulate traffic on all streets and bridges; prohibit encroachments or obstacles thereon, and 5 SECTION 21(d) - (d) Any city, municipality, or barangay may, by a duly enacted ordinance, temporarily close and regulate the use of any local street, road, thoroughfare, or any other public place where shopping malls, Sunday, flea or night markets, or shopping areas may be established and where goods, merchandise, foodstuffs, commodities, or articles of commerce may be sold and dispensed to the general public.

when necessary in the interest of public welfare, authorize the removal or encroachments and illegal constructions in public places; xxx xxx xxx Therefore, the barangay's power to regulate its own streets is limited to the activities set forth under Section 21(d) of the LGC. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly.
